title: Command S on a video edit does what the user picks
goal: Once a video edit can be saved as a project, Command S has to mean one thing on it. The user picks whether it always saves the project, or writes a plain trim of one recording back over that recording as the old recording window did, and this task builds that answer.
notes: Replaces the withdrawn card on trim-becomes-a-tool-and-the-recording-window-ret (2026-09-20), which asked about one trimmed recording with an arrow on it. Depends on a-video-edit-can-be-saved-as-a-project-and-opene for the project format. Code: EditorState.saveDocument / saveAffordance / SaveAffordance.forDocument (PhotonzCore). The old recording window's write-back path lives in the recording window code that trim-becomes-a-tool retires; option b reuses it for the one-untouched-clip case.
acceptance: Command S on an edited video does what the answered card says, at Next defaults, with no switch changed
The File menu, the edited dot and the close sheet agree with it (SaveAffordance stays the one answer they all read)
A walk presses Command S on a cut, multi-clip edit and on a plain trim of one recording, and checks what landed on disk
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Waiting on the card: what Command S does on a video edit
decision "You cut a recording, dropped in a second clip, music and a title. What should Command S do?" resolved: Command S saves the project

adversarial pass before building: the card chose a (Command S saves the project). A Premiere editor pressing Command S on an untitled project gets a save box, then saves in place from then on; that is what this builds for a recording that has never been saved. Stops for a first-time user: none new, Save was dimmed before and is now live and opens the ordinary save box. Mock check: no video mock draws a save box or a close sheet (standard macOS); the title bar name/size/length/saved line is already filed as a-video-window-says-its-name-size-length-and-whe. Plan: SaveAffordance gets a case for an edited recording never saved anywhere (Save live, close asks with Save and Export beside it), the dimmed-Save case goes, the close sheet becomes the ordinary Save sheet with Export added, Current's recording window untouched (recordings are documents only in Next).

built option a. Verified: SaveAffordanceTests rewritten first; full suite 9858 green; command-s-saves-a-video-project-walk ok at Next defaults with 6 real captures (plain trim: Command S wrote project.photonz pointing at Tutorial Sample.mp4, recording byte for byte 151020 bytes unchanged, reopened equal; multi-clip: project pointing at the recording and b-roll, then a cut and Command S saved in place, reopened equal with 3 pieces + b-roll). Also ok: a-recording-opens-in-the-editor-at-defaults-walk, a-project-whose-files-moved-walk, close-a-trimmed-recording-walk, save-is-live-after-a-trim-walk, trim-save-send-walk. a-video-edit-saves-as-a-project-walk fails at the transition picker (step 34) on main WITHOUT this change too (stashed and rerun): filed p1 clicking-a-cut-opens-the-transition-picker-again. Command S on a video saves the project (card answer a), at Next defaults: on a recording never saved, Save is live and opens the save box for a .photonz project, then saves in place; the close sheet asks Save with Export beside it; the recording is never written over.
